newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: U.S. invites Azeri leader for first official visit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. invites Azeri leader for first official visit.

text.p: The United States has invited Azerbaijan's President Haydar Aliyev to make the first official visit since the former Soviet republic gained independence in 1991, officials from both countries said on Monday.
An Azeri presidential spokesman said Aliyev's visit was likely take place in July or August. U.S. Embassy spokesman Richard Brown confirmed the invitation.

The invitation comes after recent signs that Washington would like to step up efforts to mediate a peaceful settlement of conflict around Azerbaijan's breakaway Armenian-populated region of Nagorno-Karabakh.
Azeri officials said the U.S. invitation could lead to warmer relatations and the eventual removal of U.S. legislation barring government aid until Baku resumes trade ties with Armenia.

A 1994 ceasefire ended the territorial dispute, which began when Nagorno-Karabakh broke away in the late 1980s. But a political settlement to the conflict, which killed thousands of people, is still a long way off.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright discussed the issue earlier this month during talks in Moscow.
Aliyev has twice visited the United Nations in New York, but has never been invited for an official visit to Washington.
